newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet says dangerous cargo was disguised.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet says dangerous cargo was disguised.

text.p: ValuJet Airlines Inc. alleged on Thursday that maintenance company SabreTech Corp. deliberately disguised dangerous cargo suspected in the May 1996 crash of Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades.

ValuJet said it had asked the National Transportation Safety Board to investigate this "new evidence" before issuing a final conclusion about the cause of the crash, which killed all 110 people on board the DC-9.
The NTSB is to release its final report on the crash on August 19. Preliminary reports have blamed a fire in the cargo hold that was fueled by oxygen generators carried there.
SabreTech is the federally-licensed maintenance contractor that shipped the oxygen generators on Flight 592.

"ValuJet believes there is significant evidence pointing to some SabreTech employees deliberately and deceptively packaging, mislabeling and illegally shipping cargo which they knew was dangerous ...and which they knew the airline would refuse to carry unless they misled ValuJet employees about what they were shipping," ValuJet said.
It alleged that SabreTech personnel may have falsified the shipping ticket "because they believed the process of proper disposal and transport of the generators would take too much time."

ValuJet said it had provided its "new evidence," discovered by attorneys working for the airline, to the NTSB, the Federal Aviation Administration, the Fedaral Bureau of Investigation and the federal prosecutor in Miami.

"Significant questions related to this accident remain unanswered," the airline said in a press release. "Because of the pending criminal investigation of SabreTech and its employees, the SabreTech personnel involved with the handling, packaging and shipping of the oxygen generators have taken the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.
"As a consequence, the NTSB and the public have only gotten half the story."
SabreTech could not be reached for comment on the ValuJet allegations.

ValuJet's cargo policy prohibits the transport of oxygen generators on company aircraft. Since the crash of Flight 592, the FAA has banned carriage of oxygen generators on all passenger flights in the United States.

ValuJet alleged that a SabreTech shipping clerk, when preparing shipping documents for the oxygen generators carried aboard Flight 592, instructed another SabreTech employee to list the generators as "oxy canisters - empty."

When the generators were delivered to Flight 592 by SabreTech, they were packed without protective materials, in unmarked boxes without required warnings or other disclosures of their contents, according to the airline.
